messages:
jasper: Hey team — customer JasperHealth on dedicated-prod-us-west reporting ~15% 429s during a morning surge (started ~08:17 PST). Error body includes "scale_up_timeout" and a couple of "pod pending: attach volume" entries. They say requests queue up and then get 429. Can someone triage?

maya: on it. can you paste a failing request/response (headers + body) and the cluster name? also which model+variant?

jasper: cluster: dh-prod-usw-2, model: gptx-3-8b-quant, variant: low-latency. sample curl:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate

response (truncated):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Retry-After: 22
X-Warmup-Remaining: 1

{"error":"scale_up_timeout","details":"pending provisioning: 3 pods stuck in Pending (attach-volume)"}

maya: thanks. that X-Warmup-Remaining header is helpful. can you confirm if cluster has a warm-pool configured and the min_replicas?

jasper: warm-pool enabled but min_replicas=1, max_replicas=50. spikes are sudden from a single customer test tenant.

incidents-bot: ALERT: DedicatedPoolScaleStall detected for dh-prod-usw-2 at 2026-03-18T15:12:00Z (alert_id=INC-3427)

maya: triage notes so far: scale requests are getting to the autoscaler, but kube-level events show PodPending due to volume attach delays on new nodes (EBS attach latency ~6-12s each). overall scale-up time > 30s -> requests hit app-level throttle. escalating to eng-runtime + infra. temporary customer mitigation below.

samir: I saw the same in infra metrics — node provisioning and volume attach tail latency spiked after a cloud-spot reclaim event in the us-west pool. For immediate relief: 1) enable routing fallback to a compatible hosted variant (if allowed by customer) OR 2) increase min_replicas to 3 in that cluster while we investigate. Either will reduce future 429s during bursts.

maya: jasper — quick steps to enable fallback via Console: Settings -> Routing -> Add Rule: if model unavailable -> route to gptx-3-8b-quant-hosted (latency variant). Or, to bump min_replicas from CLI: 

# platform-cli
redwood cluster update dh-prod-usw-2 --min-replicas=3

jasper: going to enable fallback for now, also asked product owner if bumping min_replicas is ok.

zev: root cause hypothesis: autoscaler headroom calculation used recent avg token length and underestimated burst concurrency; combined with cold node attach overhead (volumes + image pulls) produced >30s ready time. two follow-ups: 1) reduce autoscaler scale_cooldown so probe-triggered scaling happens earlier? actually cooldown prevents thrash — instead we should widen headroom default and warm-pool target for high-risk clusters. 2) implement a short-lived prefetch/warm-worker that keeps hot KV caches primed to reduce per-pod init time.

maya: can eng-runtime propose a safe config change we can push as an emergency patch?

zev: yes — proposal: for dh-prod-usw-2 set autoscaler.headroom_tokens=2, autoscaler.warm_pool_min=2, pod_warmup_timeout=120s. Patch command (ops only):

kubectl patch configmap autoscaler-config -n redwood-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"dh-prod-usw-2.autoscaler.headroom_tokens":"2","dh-prod-usw-2.autoscaler.warm_pool_min":"2","dh-prod-usw-2.pod_warmup_timeout":"120"}}'

samir: ops note — increasing warm_pool_min to 2 will increase monthly cost slightly but reduce customer 429s. I'll approve for emergency window.

maya: reproduction steps for eng (what we used):
1) run k6 against /v1/generate with concurrency=40 for 180s targeting dh-prod-usw-2
2) observe scale-up requests in autoscaler logs, then check kubectl get events for PodPending: FailedAttachVolume
3) verify 429s spike in app logs within 20-40s of test start

maya: logs we pulled (redacted):
[autoscaler] 2026-03-18T15:11:55Z scale_request desired=6 current=1 reason=queued_surges
[kubelet] 2026-03-18T15:12:02Z Pod "worker-5" status: Pending - FailedAttachVolume for volume "nvme-data-xyz"
[orchestrator] 2026-03-18T15:12:30Z node-provision finished; pod ready at 32s

ops-bot: Note: ticket created in Jira INFRA-1029 and assigned to infra-team.

jasper: fallback applied, retrying customer load now. will report back in 10m. thanks for the fast triage. :pray:

samir: plan: push zev's autoscaler config patch in the next 10m (emergency), monitor 429 rate; follow up with infra to investigate cloud attach tail latencies and possible node type change. I'll post rollback steps if we need to revert.

zev: once emergency patch is in place we'll also add a health-check metric to surface attach-latency > 5s in the Console so customers & SRE can see risk early.

maya: customer update draft: "We've temporarily routed traffic to a compatible backup variant and increased warm capacity to prevent 429s. Engineering is investigating underlying node provisioning delays and will follow up with a permanent fix." -- ok to send?

jasper: send it. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-3427 | dh-prod-usw-2 scale stall | priority=P2 | owner=infra-team

maya: closing loop here after follow-up: emergency patch applied at 15:22Z, 429 rate dropped to <1% in 5m window. infra investigating node attach tail latencies; will post RCA when ready. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
